Matt Loesby

Libertarian candidate for U.S. Senator, Idaho · Challenger

Software engineer (backend systems for video games); chair of the Libertarian Party of Idaho

Matt Loesby is a software engineer from Eagle, Idaho, and chairs the Libertarian Party of Idaho. He was the Libertarian nominee for Idaho's 1st Congressional District in 2024. He filed for U.S. Senate on February 27, 2026, and won the May 19, 2026 Libertarian primary unopposed with 855 votes.

Where Loesby stands

Immigration
Supports mass deportation of people in the country illegally. Also supports the 'remigration' of foreign ethnic enclaves, saying many legal immigrants and their children must be sent back to their homelands.
Public lands
Says the federal government has no rightful role in managing state land. Supports ceding all federal land in Idaho to the State of Idaho.
Energy prices
Proposes removing regulations that he says block the building of nuclear power plants for base-load power. Says solar should be an option for people who want to live off the grid.
Water and the Columbia River Treaty
Says the best way to preserve water for civilian and farm use is to avoid selling it to Oregon, Washington and California, and to keep Idaho's rainfall in Idaho.
Cost of living and housing
Says affordability depends on ending deficit spending. Proposes major cuts to entitlements, including Social Security, and an end to funding for overseas military operations.
Medicaid and SNAP
Calls for undoing the programs of the Progressive Era, the New Deal and the Great Society, and for aggressive cuts to mandatory spending on what he calls wealth transfer programs.
Iran war
Supports pulling U.S. forces out of all foreign conflicts, including the military conflict with Iran. Supports withdrawing all American troops to the U.S. homeland.
Russia and Ukraine
Says the U.S. should withdraw from all global institutions, including the U.N., NATO and Interpol, and handle diplomacy one country at a time.
Abortion
Opposes Proposition 1. Supports state-level abortion bans with an exception only to save the life of the mother, and calls abortion an act of homicide.
Agriculture
Proposes cutting laws and regulations that he says push farmers and ranchers away from the best uses of their land and livestock.

Background

  • Libertarian nominee for U.S. Senate, Idaho, 2026 (won primary unopposed, May 19, 2026)
  • Libertarian nominee, Idaho's 1st Congressional District, 2024
